flowchart_decision_nodes.question: If not decompensated HF
flowchart_decision_nodes.if_no: Beta blockers, verapamil, or diltiazem (Class 1); Digoxin (2a); Amiodarone (2b)

adjunct_recommendations: Addition of magnesium to AV nodal blockade (2a)
Note: verapamil/diltiazem contraindicated in patients with moderate-severe LV dysfunction regardless of decompensated HF (see footnote)
evidence_summary: Intravenous amiodarone shown to be effective in controlling ventricular rates in critically ill patients; retrospective studies reported significant heart rate decrease without BP decrease compared with IV diltiazem and digoxin.

One randomized study of critically ill AF patients compared diltiazem infusion, amiodarone bolus/infusion, and amiodarone regimen; diltiazem allowed better rate control over 24 hours but was associated with higher hypotension requiring discontinuation.

Limited data for non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers (eg, diltiazem) in HFrEF due to presumed negative inotropic effects; retrospective analyses show increased morbidity (eg, acute kidney injury within 48 hours, increased HF worsening) in patients with LVEF ≤50% receiving diltiazem.
levels_of_evidence_seen_on_page: Class 1 (direct current cardioversion; beta blockers/verapamil/diltiazem when not decompensated HF)
Class 2a (digoxin; addition of magnesium to AV nodal blockade)
Class 2b (IV amiodarone in decompensated HF; amiodarone for rate control)
Class 3 (harm) for verapamil/diltiazem in decompensated HF or moderate-severe LV dysfunction
important_notes: Asterisk: verapamil/diltiazem contraindicated in patients with moderate-severe LV dysfunction regardless of decompensated HF
Abbreviations on page: AF (atrial fibrillation), AV (atrioventricular), HF (heart failure), LV (left ventricular), LVEF (left ventricular ejection fraction), RVR (rapid ventricular response)
